initial_response.final_answer: 검색된 자료에서 답변을 뒷받침할 직접 근거를 확인하지 못했습니다.

frozen_criteria.description: The operational research should clearly define the conventional normal resistivity tool and its components, specifically identifying the AM spacing as the distance between two electrodes.

The research should provide a detailed explanation of the conventional normal resistivity tool's configuration, including the roles and positions of all electrodes involved in the AM spacing measurement.
The operational research should include a reference to the standard definitions or industry guidelines that describe the AM spacing in the context of resistivity logging tools.
The research should demonstrate an understanding of how the AM spacing influences the resistivity measurement and the interpretation of geological formations.

In the conventional resistivity logging tools currents are passed through the formation 
by means of current electrodes and voltages are measured between measure electrodes. 
These measured voltages provide the resistivity determination for each device.
In an homogeneous, isotropic formation of infinite extent, the equipotential surfaces 
surrounding a single current emitting electrode (A) are spheres.  The voltage between 
the electrode (M) situated on one of these spheres and one at infinity is proportional 
to the resistivity of the homogeneous formation, and the measured voltage can be 
scaled in resistivity units.
In the normal device (Figure 20), a current of constant intensity is passed between 
two electrodes, A and B.  The resultant potential difference is measured between 
two other electrodes, M and N.  Electrodes A and M are on the sonde.  B and N are, 
theoretically, located an infinite distance away.  In practice, B is the cable armor, and 
N is an electrode on the bridle (the insulation-covered lower end of the cable) far 
removed from A and M.  The distance AM is called the spacing (16-in. spacing for 
the short normal, 64-in. spacing for the long normal), and th

of low-permeability matrix.  Therefore, 
only a small portion of the total original formation fluids (formation water and, if 
present, hydrocarbons) is displaced by the filtrate - even very close to the borehole.  
In this case, no true flushed zone exists.
Many sophisticated resistivity logging methods have been developed to measure 
the resistivity of the flushed zone, Rxo, and the resistivity of the uninvaded virgin 
zone, Rt.
7.3 Conventional Electrical Tools
The deep, medium and shallow resistivity tools are generally run in combination.  
The earliest such combination was known as the conventional electrical survey (ES) 
consists of an SP, 16”, normal, 64” normal and 18 ft 8” lateral device.
